basis: The new combined-scope-order assertion binds the four-element scope list to global, shared group, origin A and origin B. Each actor's scope identities were already independently derived and checked, so the new scope-index interpretation does not trust an unchecked producer ordering.

scopeUpdates and scopeStarts are maintained from the literal Go mutation/status schedule and independently checked profile time, not from Python expected rate fields. Only mutations advance updates; only first STARTED mutations advance start history. Replays, errors, blocked claims and maintenance leave these expectations unchanged.

The direct assertions aggregate both actors for global/group counters and select the owning actor for each origin. They check active=pending+started, pending/started counts, concurrency 2 for global and 1 elsewhere, zero intervals, global deadline 0, and group/origin deadlines equal to their latest actual start.

updated_at_ms and rate_scopes inventory scores must match the last scope mutation. Unmaterialized origin hashes remain absent until their first successful claim; zero is a valid unmaterialized sentinel because all fixed profile times are positive.

Cancelled A retains zero origin start/deadline history while B later starts. Label-based origin attribution also remains correct in the reversed profile; equal-millisecond profiles preserve the same arithmetic without requiring strictly increasing timestamps.

basis: The new test shifts all observed numeric times by 200000 ms while preserving null error timestamps, then sets the final observation end to first observation start+30000. This asserts acceptance of the exact measurement-span boundary after a setup delay.

The resulting start/end are 1200001 and 1230001, below the setup-relative case deadline 1300000 and both lease deadlines. The +1 ms variant therefore isolates SHARED_MEASURE_SPAN rather than failing the case or lease bounds.
Appending a 22nd observation explicitly requires SHARED_OBSERVATIONS, and removing now_ms from the known error step requires rejection rather than accepting missing as explicit null.

The 200000 ms setup delay differs from the original recommendation's illustrative 270000 ms delay but satisfies its purpose: independently preserving the measurement-span boundary and strict observation/prefix shapes.
